papers.title: Phenomenological Chiral Effective Field Theory for Neutrino Event Generators
papers.abstract: Single-pion production is a crucial interaction channel for accelerator-based neutrino experiments, which rely on neutrino event generators for its cross sections. However, no model implemented in current generators provides a consistent and systematically improvable description of the resonance region. In this work, we develop a phenomenological chiral effective field theory model of pion production, built from nucleons, pions, and the $\Delta(1232)$ with consistent, spin 3/2, gauge-invariant couplings, and we implement it in a fully automated pipeline from the Lagrangian to events using FeynRules, UFO 2.0, and Sherpa. We validate our results with pion photoproduction data and compare against neutrino bubble chamber, MINERvA, T2K, MicroBooNE, MiniBooNE, and electron-carbon scattering data. The framework can be systematically improved by extending the Lagrangian with higher-order operators and additional degrees of freedom, and by refitting couplings and form factors as new data become available. Combined with nuclear model interfaces, our approach opens a path to resonance-region predictions that meet the needs of next-generation experiments.
papers.reason: Develops a phenomenological chiral effective field theory model for pion production with Delta(1232) and implements it in event generators, perfectly aligned with the reader's core interests. [favorite author: Isaacson]

summary.tldr: A phenomenological chiral effective field theory model of single-pion production incorporating the $\Delta(1232)$ resonance and coherent non-resonant backgrounds is automated via FeynRules, UFO 2.0, and Sherpa for neutrino event generators.
summary.novel_idea: Unlike existing generator models that add resonance and non-resonant contributions incoherently or rely on precomputed tables, this approach derives all tree-level amplitudes from a single chiral Lagrangian with gauge-invariant spin-3/2 couplings, maintaining automatic CVC/PCAC consistency and enabling fully automated event generation for arbitrary electroweak probes.
summary.method: The framework utilizes a two-flavor chiral Lagrangian with nucleons, pions, and a Rarita-Schwinger $\Delta(1232)$, implementing empirical form factors at the vertex level through UFO 2.0. Sherpa evaluates tree-level matrix elements, which are interfaced with Achilles for nuclear initial states (spectral functions) and impact-parameter cascade final-state interactions.
key_results: Free-nucleon pion photoproduction cross sections are reproduced within $\sim 10\%$ across threshold and resonance regions.
The axial $N\to\Delta$ coupling is predicted with $C_5^A(0) = 1.27$ from first-principles relations.

Nuclear-target calculations on carbon and argon successfully capture the $\Delta$ peak structure and significantly improve T2K and MicroBooNE/MINERvA cross section comparisons when an energy-dependent $\Delta$ width is included.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly impacts your core interest in neutrino event generators (GENIE, NuWro, Achilles) and nucleon axial form factors by providing the first systematically improvable, automated chiral-EFT alternative to outdated resonance models for DUNE and Hyper-K oscillation analyses.
summary.caveats: Higher-mass resonances ($>1.4$ GeV), vector mesons, and two-body current/in-medium $\Delta$ modifications are omitted in this version.

papers.title: Incorporating deep neural networks into lepton-nucleus interaction modeling
papers.abstract: We present a scheme to incorporate precise inclusive cross-section predictions from a deep neural network trained on electron--carbon scattering data into a Monte Carlo event generator. The inclusive prediction is decomposed into independent exclusive interaction channels using the generator's theoretical models, and the resulting events are reweighted accordingly. We apply this scheme to investigate nuclear effects in inclusive and semi-exclusive electron-scattering measurements.
papers.reason: Inorporates precise inclusive electron-carbon deep learning predictions into a Monte Carlo event generator via exclusive channel decomposition, sitting squarely in the reader's core expertise. [favorite author: Jan Sobczyk]

summary.tldr: A new framework named $e$WroNet incorporates deep neural network predictions of inclusive electron-carbon cross sections into the NuWro event generator by reweighting exclusive theoretical channels.
summary.novel_idea: Bridges the gap between data-driven machine learning inclusive cross-section fits and event-by-event Monte Carlo generators by decomposing inclusive DNN predictions into exclusive reaction channels using theoretical models.
summary.method: The inclusive cross-section predictions from a bootstrap-trained deep neural network on electron-carbon scattering are mapped onto NuWro's exclusive channels (quasielastic scattering via spectral functions, an approximate meson-exchange current model, and $\Delta$-resonance single-pion production) via event reweighting.
key_results: The $e$WroNet scheme reproduces inclusive SLAC electron-carbon cross-section data up to the upper boundary of the $\Delta$ resonance region.

Comparison with CLAS $e4\nu$ pionless $(e,e^\prime)_{0\pi}$ data reveals that predictions match the rising edge of the QE peak but lie $15\%$ to $30\%$ below data at the QE and $\Delta$ peaks, respectively.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly relates to electron scattering constraints on neutrino cross sections and event generator development (NuWro), offering a novel pathway to utilize ML surrogate models for nuclear response functions.
summary.caveats: The approach assumes incoherent channel separation, ignoring quantum-mechanical interference between one- and two-body currents, and is currently restricted kinematically to the $\Delta$ region below higher resonance thresholds.

papers.title: Meson spectroscopy from lattice QCD
papers.abstract: Determining the meson spectrum directly from Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) remains a central challenge, since QCD is strongly coupled at low energies and most excited states appear as resonances in hadronic decay channels. Advances in lattice QCD and scattering theory now provide a systematic framework for extracting meson spectra and resonance properties from first principles. Here I present an overview of this program and review current state-of-the-art calculations in meson spectroscopy from lattice QCD. I highlight recent progress in the extraction of resonant and coupled-channel amplitudes, along with frontier developments in three-body dynamics and the determination of meson photo-couplings. Together, these advances are bringing us closer to a comprehensive first-principles description of the excited meson spectrum.
papers.reason: Reviews first-principles extraction of meson spectra, resonance properties, and coupled-channel amplitudes from lattice QCD, highly relevant to axial form factors and interaction models.

summary.tldr: This review summarizes recent advancements in extracting meson spectra, resonance properties, and photocouplings from first-principles lattice QCD using finite-volume scattering frameworks.
summary.novel_idea: Highlights the maturation of Lüscher finite-volume methods into coupled-channel dynamics, explicit left-hand cut inclusion, and relativistic three-body formalisms for excited meson resonances.
summary.method: Surveys lattice QCD methodologies including variational methods with distillation, quantization conditions mapping finite-volume discrete energy levels to infinite-volume two- and three-hadron K-matrices, and $2+\mathcal{J}\to 2$ transition formalisms for electroweak form factors.
key_results: Successful determination of coupled-channel charmonium resonance parameters (e.g., $D\bar{D}$, $D_s\bar{D}_s$, $D^*\bar{D}^*$) and subthreshold pole structures.
Progress in three-pion scattering amplitudes ($I=2, J^P=1^+$) yielding quantitative Dalitz distribution analyses.
summary.why_it_matters: Relevant to your high-interest areas in lattice QCD inputs for hadron dynamics, though focused on meson spectroscopy rather than direct nucleon electroweak form factors.
summary.caveats: Calculations often rely on unphysical quark masses (heavier than physical pion masses) and neglect lattice spacing artifacts in simplified implementations.

papers.title: Search for long-lived heavy neutral leptons in signatures with one prompt muon and a secondary vertex formed by two non-prompt muons in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 and 13.6 TeV
papers.abstract: A search for heavy neutral leptons (HNLs) in the decay of W bosons is performed in final states with three muons, with one originating promptly from the primary interaction vertex and the other two stemming from a common secondary vertex. The analyzed proton-proton collision data correspond to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$ recorded at a centre-of-mass energy of 13 TeV in 2016$-$2018, and of 34.6 fb$^{-1}$ recorded at 13.6 TeV in 2022. The analysis strategy is optimized for large HNL decay lengths by requiring highly non-prompt muons forming a secondary vertex far from the beam line, and hence reconstructed only in the muon system of the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC. This enhances the analysis reach in the high HNL lifetime region, corresponding to low HNL masses (2$-$4 GeV) and small mixing parameters with the standard model neutrinos (10$^{-6}$$-$10$^{-5}$), where prompt and tracker-based non-prompt analyses have limited acceptance. No excess over the background prediction is found. Under the Majorana HNL hypothesis, exclusion limits at 95\% confidence level are set on the HNL mixing parameter as functions of the HNL mass in the range of 1$-$5 GeV.
papers.reason: Searches for long-lived heavy neutral leptons in three-muon final states with displaced vertices using CMS data, directly relevant to BSM searches at collider/neutrino facilities.

summary.tldr: CMS search for long-lived heavy neutral leptons (HNLs) in three-muon final states utilizing purely outer-muon-system tracking extends sensitivity to long-lifetime regimes.
summary.novel_idea: Targets low-mass ($2-4$ GeV) and small-mixing ($10^{-6}-10^{-5}$) Majorana HNLs by vetoing inner tracker information on displaced muons, explicitly probing transverse decay lengths up to 4 meters.
summary.method: Analyzed $138\text{ fb}^{-1}$ at $13$ TeV (2016-2018) and $34.6\text{ fb}^{-1}$ at $13.6$ TeV (2022) proton-proton collisions by selecting one prompt muon and a secondary vertex formed by two displaced standalone (DSA) muons, with background estimated via an ABCD data-driven method.
key_results: No significant excess over Standard Model background predictions was observed.
New 95% confidence level exclusion limits were set on the HNL mixing parameter $|V_{\mu N}|^2$ as a function of mass, surpassing previous experimental results for masses between $2.5$ and $4.2$ GeV.
summary.why_it_matters: Directly touches on BSM physics searches at collider neutrino and precision facilities, specifically long-lived particle signatures and heavy neutral lepton mixing parameters.
summary.caveats:
Assumes single-family mixing dominance ($
u_	au$ and $
u_e$ mixing set to zero); multi-family mixing scenarios weaken these specific limits.

papers.title: Color transparency effects on the deuteron spin observables in the hard $pd \to ppn$ reaction
papers.abstract: The pionless breakup of a deuteron induced by 15 GeV/$c$ beam proton is considered theoretically in the kinematics where both outgoing protons are fast and the neutron is slow in the rest frame of the deuteron. Significant influence of color transparency on the deuteron vector and tensor analyzing powers is expected.
papers.reason: Theoretical analysis of color transparency effects on deuteron spin observables and analyzing powers in high-energy pd -> ppn breakup.

summary.tldr: Color transparency (CT) effects are predicted to significantly modify deuteron vector (DVAP) and tensor (DTAP) analyzing powers in hard $pd \to ppn$ breakup reactions at $15$ GeV/$c$.
summary.novel_idea: Extends previous color transparency studies in hard deuteron breakup from single tensor components ($A_{zz}$) to the full set of DVAP and DTAP tensor components within the generalized eikonal approximation.
summary.method: Calculations employ the generalized eikonal approximation (GEA) including multi-step soft rescattering of incoming and outgoing protons on the spectator neutron, with CT incorporated via the quantum diffusion model.
key_results: Initial- and final-state interactions (ISI/FSI) shift the extrema of the tensor components from $p_{st} \simeq 0.3$ down to $0.2$ GeV/$c$.
Color transparency effects grow with spectator transverse momentum ($p_{st}$), producing strong variations in angular and momentum dependencies most pronounced around $p_{st} \simeq 0.3$ GeV/$c$.
summary.why_it_matters: Bridges electron/proton scattering nuclear probes, final-state interactions (FSI), and color transparency mechanisms relevant to high-energy nuclear targets and future NICA/Nuclotron measurements.
summary.caveats: Calculations assume specific quantum diffusion parameters ($\Delta M^2 \approx 1-3 \text{ GeV}^2$) which carry ongoing theoretical uncertainties.

papers.title: Neutrino Oscillation in a Static Dihole Geometry
papers.abstract: We investigate neutrino flavor oscillations in the static equal-mass Majumdar-Papapetrou dihole geometry, restricting the propagation to the symmetry plane. Within the null approximation, we derive the leading contribution to the neutrino phase and numerically evaluate the geodesic integrals. For two neutrino flavors, interference between different trajectories introduces a dependence on the individual neutrino masses and on the neutrino mass ordering for nonmaximal mixing. We analyze the transition probability in different spacetime configurations possessing two light rings, a merged light ring (critical configuration), and no light rings in the equatorial plane. In the weak-lensing regime, the transition probability generally increases with the black holes' individual masses, while variations in the half-separation produce no qualitative change in the transition probability. In stronger-lensing configurations, variations in both the mass and half-separation modify the heights and positions of the extrema, with no monotonic increase or decrease in the transition probability. For the critical and no-light-ring configurations studied, we identify three zero-winding trajectories connecting the source and detector, including one passing near the symmetry axis. The probability remains oscillatory, and its oscillatory pattern depends strongly on the neutrino energy.
papers.topic: Neutrino Oscillations in Black Hole Spacetime
papers.reason: Investigates neutrino flavor oscillations in a static dihole geometry, connecting general relativistic spacetime effects to neutrino wave mechanics.

summary.tldr: The paper investigates neutrino flavor oscillations in an equal-mass Majumdar-Papapetrou dihole spacetime using the null approximation, finding that path interference introduces sensitivity to individual neutrino masses and mass ordering.
summary.novel_idea: Unlike standard single-path vacuum oscillations which depend solely on mass-squared differences, this work computes multi-path interference in a binary black hole spacetime, showing that relative phases between geodesics encode individual neutrino absolute masses and mass hierarchy signatures.
summary.method: The authors solve the Dirac equation in the eikonal limit within the tetrad formalism, deriving the covariant phase along null geodesics in the symmetry plane of an equal-mass Majumdar-Papapetrou dihole. They numerically evaluate geodesic integrals for weak-, critical-, and strong-lensing configurations with varying light-ring structures.
key_results: Derived closed-form expressions for purely radial motion and evaluated transition probabilities for zero-winding trajectories across three light-ring configurations.
Demonstrated that transition probabilities remain oscillatory and energy-dependent, with separation effects becoming more prominent in strong-lensing regimes.
summary.why_it_matters: Provides a rigorous curved-spacetime framework for how gravitational lensing and multi-path interference affect neutrino flavor evolution, directly intersecting with theoretical studies of astrophysical neutrino propagation in compact object spacetimes.
summary.caveats: The analysis is restricted to zero-winding trajectories within the symmetry plane for two neutrino flavors, omitting higher windings, chaotic non-equatorial orbits, and wave-packet decoherence effects.

papers.title: Layered Wire-Grid Haloscope for Millielectronvolt Axions and Dark Photons
papers.abstract: We propose MADGRID (Millielectronvolt Axions and Dark photons with layered GRIDs), a few wire grids in front of a mirror, tuned by their spacing, forming an epsilon-near-zero slab that radiates through its face into external optics. Unlike wire-plasma haloscopes, the signal need not cross the lossy medium to reach an antenna, and metal grids replace the disks of dielectric haloscopes. A 1 m$^2$ array in 10 T could probe axion-photon couplings below the CAST bound up to 1.4 meV with kinetic-inductance detectors, and KSVZ couplings over 0.8-3.9 meV with future photon counters. Without a magnet, it could probe dark photon mixings down to $3.4\times10^{-16}$.
papers.reason: Proposes a layered wire-grid haloscope (MADGRID) to search for millielectronvolt axions and dark photons.

summary.tldr: MADGRID proposes a layered wire-grid haloscope backed by a mirror to form an epsilon-near-zero slab that radiates millielectronvolt axion and dark photon signals directly into external optics.
summary.novel_idea: Instead of utilizing internal lossy media where signals must propagate to a localized antenna, MADGRID stacks free-standing wire grids a quarter-wavelength apart in front of a mirror, allowing the axion-induced signal to radiate straight through its face into external optics.
summary.method: The author models the wire grid stack as an impedance sheet boundary-value problem, calculating the Drude-like plasma response, material and unloaded quality factors, anomalous skin-effect copper surface resistances, and single-mode Gaussian optical collection efficiency.
key_results: A 1 m^2 array in a 10 T field paired with kinetic-inductance detectors can probe axion-photon couplings below the CAST bound up to 1.4 meV.
Future photon counters could cover KSVZ couplings over 0.8-3.9 meV, while magnet-less configurations can probe dark photon mixings down to 3.4 x 10^-16.
summary.why_it_matters: Offers a highly innovative detector design for exploring the well-motivated but experimentally difficult millielectronvolt axion dark matter window without the severe internal attenuation limits of traditional wire-plasma haloscopes.
summary.caveats: The performance forecasts depend on in-field THz surface impedance behavior in extreme anomalous skin-effect regimes and require developing photon counters with sub-millihertz dark counts across 0.2-2 THz.

papers.title: Hadronic Molecules: Theory
papers.abstract: Since the turn of the century it becomes evident that the naive quark model is not capable to describe the rich phenomenology of hadrons, especially in the doubly heavy sector. For a large number of those states a molecular structure appears to be a natural description. In these proceedings I review the theory of hadronic molecules, how they can be described systematically in effective field theories and what imprint this structure leaves in observables. On two examples I explain non-trivial predictions emerging from the molecular hypothesis that can be tested in future experiments and lattice QCD calculations, promising deep insights into the inner workings of QCD.
papers.reason: Reviews the effective field theory description of hadronic molecules and non-trivial predictions for QCD dynamics.

summary.tldr: This review summarizes the effective field theory description of hadronic molecules, focusing on Weinberg's compositeness criterion and recent developments regarding heavy quark spin symmetry and isospin breaking partners.
summary.novel_idea: It systematically connects near-threshold hadronic poles to universal molecular properties using EFTs, highlighting how heavy quark spin symmetry and isospin violation successfully predict spin partners and hidden poles for exotics like the X(3872).
summary.method: Review of non-relativistic effective field theory loop expansions, Weinberg's compositeness relation for field wave-function renormalizations, coupled-channel potentials, and the incorporation of heavy quark spin symmetry (HQSS) and chiral EFT constraints to fit recent high-precision LHCb data.
key_results: Demonstrated that vector charmonium-like systems and X(3872) isovector partners emerge naturally as non-trivial predictions of the molecular hypothesis.
Showed that natural isospin violation in the molecular model requires an additional pole just above the D+ D*- threshold, explaining line-shape differences in B decays.
summary.why_it_matters: Provides essential theoretical foundations and EFT tools for understanding near-threshold multi-quark states and hadronic interactions, which mirror the low-energy nuclear and hadronic dynamics foundational to neutrino-nucleus interaction physics.
summary.caveats: The predictive power relies on truncation schemes and precise input data for coupled-channel branchings; separating pure molecular structures from compact core components remains challenging in deeper bound states.

papers.title: Probing dark sector with decihertz gravitational wave observations of compact binary inspirals in IndIGO-D
papers.abstract: We investigate the potential of decihertz gravitational-wave (GW) observations of compact-binary inspirals to probe atomic dark matter (aDM) and its interactions through an ultralight massive dark photon. We consider a scenario in which neutron stars accumulate DM charged under a dark Abelian massive vector mediator, leading to an additional long-range Yukawa interaction between compact objects and associated dipolar radiation. In this framework, the GW waveform acquires characteristic corrections parameterized by the Yukawa coupling strength $\alpha$, the dipole-radiation parameter $\gamma$, and a parameter related to the mediator mass $\mu$. These corrections include a leading $-1$ post-Newtonian dipole contribution and finite-mediator-mass effects. We relate the aDM corrections to existing parameterized tests of general relativity and perform Bayesian parameter-estimation analyses for simulated binary neutron star (BNS) and neutron star-black hole (NSBH) systems incorporating the modified binary inspiral in a proposed space-based decihertz detector, named IndIGO-D. For a GW170817-like BNS with nonzero aDM couplings chosen near current observational bounds, we find that the dark-photon rest energy can be inferred with a $90\%$ credible uncertainty of $O(10^{-20})\,\mathrm{eV}$, conditional on a detectable dark-sector contribution. Analyses with weaker dark-sector interactions $(\alpha \lesssim O(10^{-8}))$ show that the mediator mass remains unconstrained when both the Yukawa coupling and dipole-radiation contribution are negligible, but can be measured even for a negligible Yukawa coupling if the dipole-radiation contribution is sufficiently strong. Our results demonstrate that future decihertz GW observatories can serve as powerful laboratories for testing dark-sector physics and probing dark matter interactions in compact binaries through precision GW measurements.
papers.reason: Explores dark matter and dark photons using decihertz gravitational waves from neutron star binaries, connecting to dark sector models.

summary.tldr: The paper investigates probing atomic dark matter charged under a dark photon in compact binary inspirals using the proposed IndIGO-D decihertz gravitational-wave detector.
summary.novel_idea: Utilizes the decihertz frequency band to capture negative post-Newtonian $-2$PN Yukawa and $-1$PN dipole-radiation corrections alongside kinematic activation thresholds of dark-photon radiation channels during binary inspirals.
summary.method: Constructed a frequency-domain stationary phase approximation waveform incorporating conservative Yukawa interactions and dissipative dark-photon emission with piecewise phase matching across activation thresholds, followed by Bayesian parameter estimation via relative binning.
key_results: For a GW170817-like BNS system observed in IndIGO-D, the Yukawa coupling $\alpha$, dipole parameter $\gamma$, and mass parameter $\mu$ are constrained with 90% credible uncertainties of $3.0 \times 10^{-5}$, $1.4 \times 10^{-7}$, and $1.5 \times 10^{-9}$, respectively.
The dark-photon rest energy can be inferred with an absolute uncertainty of order $10^{-20}$ eV conditional on a detectable dark-sector signal.
summary.why_it_matters: Demonstrates how decihertz gravitational wave observations can uniquely access ultralight dark-sector physics through precision waveform modeling of negative PN terms, expanding BSM search capabilities beyond ground-based limits.
summary.caveats: Results depend heavily on the astrophysical viability of neutron stars retaining net dark charges against repulsive dark-vector forces, and the analysis assumes idealized stationary Gaussian noise models.

papers.title: Nuclear-geometry-tagging events in high-energy Ne--Ne collisions
papers.abstract: Nucleon-nucleon interactions within atomic nuclei give rise to collective properties such as deformation and nuclear clustering. Ultrarelativistic nucleon-nucleon collisions offer a novel way to probe the many-body correlations of the incoming nuclei, as the nuclear structure is reflected in the initial geometry of the produced system. State-of-the-art low-energy nuclear theory calculations predict highly deformed $^{20}$Ne nuclei with a characteristic $\alpha$+$^{16}$O bowling-pin-like shape. Since such nuclei have recently been collided at the LHC, investigating methods to maximise the sensitivity to the nuclear structure is pertinent. In this paper, we investigate whether body--body and tip--tip configurations of $^{20}$Ne nuclei can be identified in Monte--Carlo Glauber simulations using geometry-sensitive observables: the eccentricity, $\varepsilon_2$, and the transverse compactness, $d_\perp$. The nuclear configurations are obtained from nuclear lattice effective field theory calculations within the framework of Nuclear Lattice Effective Field Theory (NLEFT) and $\textit{ab initio}$ Projected Generator Coordinate Method (PGCM). We utilise a Fisher linear discriminant to select body--body and tip--tip configurations based on the $\varepsilon_2$-$d_\perp$ correlation. With classifier thresholds chosen to retain $30\%$ of the target class in a validation sample, the two-variable Fisher selection obtains purities in NLEFT (PGCM) of $0.201$ ($0.156$) and $0.573$ ($0.540$) for body--body and tip--tip events, respectively.
papers.reason: Evaluates Neon-20 nuclear deformation using NLEFT and PGCM, relevant for initial-state geometry in high-energy and nuclear interactions.

summary.tldr: The paper demonstrates that body-body and tip-tip configurations in ultrarelativistic ^20Ne-^20Ne collisions can be effectively tagged using a Fisher linear discriminant on initial eccentricity and transverse compactness.
summary.novel_idea: Combines state-of-the-art ab initio Nuclear Lattice Effective Field Theory (NLEFT) and Projected Generator Coordinate Method (PGCM) nuclear geometries with initial-state geometry-tagging via a two-variable Fisher selection to isolate bowling-pin alpha-cluster orientations.
summary.method: Performed Monte-Carlo Glauber simulations of ^20Ne-^20Ne collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 5.36$ TeV using NLEFT and PGCM density configurations, evaluating participant elliptic eccentricity $\varepsilon_2$ and inverse transverse size fluctuations $d_\perp$ for central events.
key_results: A two-variable Fisher linear discriminant with a 30% validation efficiency cut achieved purities of 0.201 (NLEFT) / 0.156 (PGCM) for body-body events and 0.573 (NLEFT) / 0.540 (PGCM) for tip-tip events.
Confirmed that nuclear deformation sensitivity persists down to $N_{\mathrm{part}} \sim 13$, well outside purely head-on collisions.
summary.why_it_matters: Links ab initio microscopic nuclear structure calculations directly to ultrarelativistic heavy-ion initial-state observables, offering new event-shape engineering strategies to test nuclear clustering at colliders.
summary.caveats: The study relies on initial-state Monte-Carlo Glauber models and toy response mappings rather than full dynamical viscous hydrodynamic simulations with explicit non-linear response.

papers.title: Monopole-Fermion Scattering from Twisted Conformal Boundary States
papers.abstract: We derive monopole-fermion scattering correlators from conformal boundary states in twisted sectors. The key ingredient is that symmetry-preserving boundary conditions contain sectors twisted by topological symmetry lines. Their overlaps determine correlators of operators attached to these lines, including the outgoing excitations required by charge conservation in the Callan-Rubakov effect. We construct the twisted boundary states of $N$ free Dirac fermions with $U(1)^N$-preserving boundary conditions, extending the familiar description in terms of charge lattices to shifted lattices describing twisted sectors. Using cluster decomposition and open-closed duality, we determine their coefficients and fix their normalization relative to the untwisted boundary state. We find that the Callan-Rubakov boundary condition yields a two-point function between an incoming fermion and an outgoing defect operator with a coefficient of unit modulus, even when the corresponding correlators of ordinary local fermions vanish. Finally, we relate these correlators to four-dimensional partial-wave scattering using gauge-covariant asymptotic states. We identify the missing $s$-wave contribution to the unitarity relation and argue that the twisted channel supplies it with precisely the required normalization.
papers.reason: Derives monopole-fermion scattering correlators and the Callan-Rubakov effect using twisted conformal boundary states.

papers.title: Transverse momentum correlations and QED effects in TMD determinations
papers.abstract: Extractions of the non-perturbative, transverse momentum dependent (TMD) hadron's structure from experimental measurements of vector-boson spectra at hadron colliders are strongly influenced by correlations across boson's transverse momentum bins and by Quantum Electrodynamics (QED) effects, both from photon emission and from the photon-photon collision background. We present a Monte Carlo framework to take this into account, and illustrate the results with a comparison of theoretical predictions with the high-precision LHCb measurements of $Z$-boson production in the forward rapidity region. We discuss the relationship with the CMS data set at central rapidities.
papers.reason: Presents a Monte Carlo framework for transverse momentum dependent parton distributions incorporating QED corrections and bin correlations.

papers.title: Stars Can Quench Superradiance Around Supermassive Black Holes
papers.abstract: Light scalar fields trigger an instability around rotating black holes which drives the rapid growth of high-density bound states on astrophysically short timescales---a phenomenon known as black hole superradiance. This process is usually tacitly assumed to happen independent of the local environment. Around supermassive black holes, however, orbiting stars and compact objects act as a perturbation that drains energy from the cloud, potentially preventing its formation altogether. In this work, we quantify under what conditions this happens, focusing on bound-free state transitions. We first compute the rate of energy dissipation due to gravitational interactions, finding that the superradiance growth rate almost always dominates the environmental depletion. The two rates are, however, close enough that the conclusion could be overturned once bound-bound transitions are included. Also, the environment dissipates the cloud faster than gravitational-wave emission, implying that stellar environments must be accounted for in a variety of indirect search strategies. We then investigate the impact of the scalar's quadratic couplings to nucleons and electromagnetism, showing that these interactions can greatly enhance energy dissipation, preventing the cloud's formation. This work highlights the importance of accounting for the local environment in studies of superradiance around intermediate and supermassive black holes.
papers.reason: Quantifies how environmental stars and scalar quadratic couplings quench superradiance around supermassive black holes.

papers.title: Phase transition dynamics of Abelian-Higgs vortices in the oscillating axion background
papers.abstract: We investigate the effect of an oscillating axion background on thermally induced vortex-antivortex production in the Abelian-Higgs model. Through its coupling to the gauge field, the axion sources an electromagnetic response in the presence of vortex magnetic flux, modifying the dynamics of the vortices. We study this system using Langevin lattice simulations with dissipation and stochastic noise. It is shown that the phase transition dynamics of Abelian-Higgs vortices, namely the pair creation of vortex and antivortex under thermal fluctuations, can be significantly modified in the oscillating axion background. We find that the axion background shifts the rapid increase in the vortex density to lower temperature. In particular, this transition temperature becomes smaller as the oscillation frequency of the axion increases. The temperature dependence of the correlation length is also modified. These features provide a new experimental approach for the axion dark matter using superconducting devices.
papers.reason: Simulates thermally induced vortex-antivortex production in the Abelian-Higgs model under an oscillating axion dark matter background.

papers.title: A first look at strange-quark polarization in top-quark decays with CMS Open Data
papers.abstract: We present a first realization of strange-quark polarimetry in top-quark decays. The longitudinal polarization of $\Lambda$ baryons is measured in the strange jets of hadronic $W\to c\bar s$ decays in semileptonic top-quark pair events, using 16.39 fb$^{-1}$ of the public CMS data of pp collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV. The $W$ decay produces the strange quark fully polarized, so that the $\Lambda$ polarization measures the transfer of the quark polarization in fragmentation. With the limited statistics available, our result is consistent both with zero and with the transfer inferred from the flavor-averaged LEP measurements. The statistical reach with the full Run-2, Run-3 and HL-LHC datasets is projected.
papers.reason: Measures Lambda baryon polarization in W -> cs decays using CMS open data to perform strange-quark polarimetry in top decays.

papers.title: Hints of self-interacting dark matter from strong gravitational lensing
papers.abstract: An analysis of 29 quadruply imaged quasars hints at dark matter halo densities consistent with gravothermal core collapse, a key prediction of self-interacting dark matter. We interpret this evidence through elastic Yukawa scattering, combining lensing with upper limits on the cross-section strength from galaxy clusters and Milky Way satellite evaporation. Favored models have dark matter masses of $20$-$80\,{\rm GeV}$, MeV-scale mediators, and Yukawa-potential strengths near $10^{-3}$, yielding cross-sections of $10^2$--$10^4 \, {\rm cm^2\,g^{-1}}$ at $10\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$. Cosmological, direct and indirect detection bounds on MeV-scale mediators motivate a neutrinophilic scalar dilepton that decays invisibly without Higgs mixing. These results demonstrate how inferences on core collapse constrain dark sector physics.
papers.reason: Analyzes strong gravitational lensing hints of self-interacting dark matter core collapse, connecting to neutrinophilic scalar mediators.

papers.title: The Importance of Curium-250 to the $\gamma$-Ray Signature of $r$-Process Remnants
papers.abstract: Identifying the astrophysical sites of the heavy rapid neutron-capture process ($r$-process) remains one of the most prominent unsolved problems in nuclear astrophysics. Emitted $\gamma$-rays from the decay of unstable nuclei have been identified as a potential observable marker on both prompt and delayed timescales which could provide conclusive evidence of the presence of $r$-process activity. In this work, we identify and discuss the importance of $^{250}$Cm to the $\gamma$-ray spectra of remnants, showing that the decay spectrum of $^{250}$Cm dominates the $\gamma$-ray spectra of $r$-process ejecta across a broad timescale ($\sim$ 2,000 - 20,000 years). We highlight the uncertain nature of this spectra: $^{250}$Cm may decay via $\alpha$-decay, $\beta$-decay, and spontaneous fission, but the decay branchings are not experimentally known, and each decay channel produces unique spectral lines which may be observable. We examine the potential for observation of the most prominent spectral signatures, finding that for conventional neutron star merger remnants, $\gamma$-ray lines will be detectable in current and future detectors only in the very near galaxy ($\sim$ 1 kpc), but other sites which could produce a larger ejecta mass may have greater observable distances. Our findings highlight the potential of actinide decay chains to indicate r-process nucleosynthesis and further underscore the necessity of measuring the nuclear properties that define their characteristic spectral signatures.
papers.reason: Investigates Curium-250 decay spectra and gamma-ray signatures from r-process remnants, offering useful nuclear decay data.

papers.title: Calorimetry as inference: the information content of particle showers and the limits of energy measurement
papers.abstract: A calorimeter does not measure the energy of a particle, it infers it from the record the absorption process leaves behind. Energy conservation writes every event as an accounting ledger, E = E_dis + E_B + E_esc + E_nu, of which only the dissipated component contributes to signal, so resolution is limited by how well the record of the dissipation constrains the missing entries. We formalize this: records form a lattice on which information is monotone; thinning a Poisson record scales Fisher information exactly by the retention; clustered records read out as sums cost the 1/(1+cv^2); and the quadrature budget a/sqrt(E) (+) b is the floor of every summed readout. The "ultimate limits" of hadronic calorimetry are identified as the first rung of a ladder, the residual spread of the invisible energy around a single correlated observable. We measure the ladder above that rung on Geant4 truth records of hadronic showers in copper, from the dissipated-energy sum to time-, position- and multiplicity-resolved records, with estimators validated on exactly solvable toy models. The achieved full-record value, model-conditional, is about 5.5%/sqrt(E) (+) 0.3% over 20-100 GeV, a factor 1.7-1.9 below the canonical one-functional construction on the same events (1.29% vs. 2.14% at 20 GeV). Under retrained high-precision neutron transport it moves from 1.29% to 1.30%, the dissipated-energy sum by 7%, and the gain from time structure becomes 0.17% in place of 0.28%. Dual-readout supplies the largest share of the information. Shower shape is next, almost entirely longitudinal, saturating at about one interaction length. Time structure adds nearly as much with or without shower shape, and stopped-muon neutrino losses set an estimated floor of 0.99% at 20 GeV. Every readout dimension has a measured information exchange rate, separating what new hardware can buy from what better algorithms can recover.
papers.reason: Formalizes information content and energy resolution limits in hadronic calorimetry using Geant4 simulations, relevant to neutrino detector physics.

papers.title: On the Role of Gravity in Supercooled Phase Transitions
papers.abstract: Theories with radiative mass generation and radiative symmetry breaking (RSB) lead to first-order phase transitions (FOPTs) and the production of gravitational waves (GWs) as well as primordial black holes if supercooling lasts long enough. Here we investigate the role of gravity in supercooled FOPTs that occur in the RSB scenario. We use a model-independent approach that is valid when a quantity (which we explicitly determine and is computable once the model is specified) is small enough. Eventually, the curvature of spacetime becomes relevant if the FOPT does not complete in the case in which gravity is ignored. We also include the effect on the FOPT of the non-minimal couplings with coefficients of zero mass dimension. Depending on such non-minimal couplings, gravity can enhance or reduce the region of parameter space where the phase transition completes. Observable consequences of the role of gravity on the FOPT that can be probed by current and future GW detectors are then worked out and we explore the possibility that the background of GWs detected by pulsar timing arrays is produced by FOPTs in the RSB scenario. We also estimate the number of e-folds that elapse when the field playing the role of the order parameter is trapped in the false vacuum, which provides important information for cosmology.
papers.reason: Studies the role of gravity in supercooled first-order phase transitions and gravitational wave production in radiative symmetry breaking.

papers.title: The Yottascale at Tera-$Z$: Petascale SUSY?
papers.abstract: As experimental and theoretical advances are made, the paradigm of grand unification faces growing challenges. In light of what has been learned at the LHC, from Higgs mass measurement and direct searches for supersymmetry, we contrast the current theoretical predictions in a simplified supersymmetric grand unified theory against present and future experimental precision, focussing on threshold corrections and renormalisation group effects above the electroweak scale. More precisely, the theoretical precision is juxtaposed to the experimental one. Especially, the impact of a future Tera-$Z$ factory such as FCC-ee is examined, while also considering the expected future improvement of proton decay constraints. We find that the improvement on the measurement of the gauge couplings expected at Tera-$Z$ will yield sensitivity to higher loop orders in the evolution of the couplings up to the Yottascale, calling for further theoretical efforts. In a minimal $\rm{SU}(5)$ scenario with nearly degenerate SUSY spectrum, we study the impact of the proton decay constraint on the SUSY scale, comparing 2- and 3-loop analyses. While the 2-loop results point to a SUSY scale around 1 PeV, the 3-loop analysis seems to exclude the model entirely. This follows from the fact that at 1-loop in the GUT threshold corrections, the mass of the colour-triplet Higgs is completely determined by the IR parameters. This \textit{IR determination} is not accidental, but rooted in the group structure and breaking of the GUT theory.
papers.reason: Examines threshold corrections and renormalisation group evolution in supersymmetric grand unified theories in light of future FCC-ee precision.

papers.title: Two-Fluid Radial Stability of Dark-Matter-Admixed Compact Objects: Dark Compact Planets, Dark White Dwarfs, Dark Neutron Stars, and Dark Oysters
papers.abstract: We investigate the equilibrium structure and stability against radial oscillations of a variety of two-fluid compact objects containing ordinary baryonic matter admixed with cold dark matter coupled through the background spacetime. For the ordinary fluid, we employ a QCD equation of state compatible with chiral effective field theory at nuclear densities (supplemented by the BPS and Negele-Vautherin models at extremely low densities) and with perturbative QCD in the high-density regime while also satisfying also current astrophysical data. For the dark fluid, we assume self-interacting fermionic matter with particle masses of $m_f=$ 2, 5, 10, and 100 GeV and two self-interaction strengths of $y=0.1$ and $10^3$. By scanning a large range of central pressures for both fluids, we identify the presence of dark compact planets, dark white dwarfs, dark neutron stars and the so-called dark oysters. Importantly, these objects are not only in two-fluid hydrostatic equilibrium, but they are also stable against two-fluid radial oscillations. We find that the relative representation of each class in the radially stable sample is strongly sensitive to the combinations of $m_f$ and $y$, with some combinations entirely suppressing some of these object classes within the sampled domain while favoring others. In addition to these classes, strong self-repulsion supports stable, dark-matter-dominated branches with compact ordinary-matter cores and extended dark halos, approaching the self-interacting fermion-star limit. Finally, we calculate the gravitational redshift at the ordinary-matter surface, $z_{\rm OM}$, including the contribution of extended dark-matter halos for which we found radially stable configurations with $z_{\rm OM}>2$.
papers.reason: Studies the equilibrium and radial stability of compact stars admixed with self-interacting fermionic dark matter across nuclear EoS.

papers.title: Reconstructing Meson Parton Distributions from Mellin Moments with Artificial Neural Networks
papers.abstract: We address the inverse problem of reconstructing a meson parton distribution function (PDF) or parton distribution amplitude (PDA) at a fixed scale from a finite set of Mellin moments. At finite moment order this map is ill posed in the Hadamard sense: the moments do not determine a unique, stable pointwise $x$-dependence, and small data perturbations can produce large changes in the reconstruction. We regularize the problem by restricting the admissible function class through constraints justified by first principles---support on $x\in[0,1]$, endpoint vanishing, unit normalization, and, for the pion, the exact $x\leftrightarrow 1-x$ symmetry---and by complementing these hard constraints with differentiable penalties that suppress the spurious multiple maxima and central concavity changes typical of ill-posed inversions. We parameterize the unknown function with two interchangeable neural cores, a multilayer perceptron (MLP) and a Kolmogorov--Arnold network (KAN), and find that the KAN reconstructs the target distributions more accurately, most markedly in the asymmetric (kaon) case. We attribute this advantage to the locality of the B-spline basis underlying the KAN, which localizes corrections during moment matching and damps the global oscillations to which the MLP is prone. Benchmarks against synthetic targets, using both ten and five input moments, support these conclusions.
papers.reason: Reconstructs meson PDFs and PDAs from Mellin moments using Kolmogorov-Arnold networks and multi-layer perceptrons with physical constraints.

papers.title: Is XTE J1814-338 a dark matter-admixed neutron star?
papers.abstract: We explore the possibility that the ultracompact object XTE J1814-338 is a dark matter-admixed neutron star (DNS) based on a general-relativistic two-fluid approach, in which one fluid describes ordinary nuclear matter and the other dark matter. The equations of state of nuclear matter and dark matter are described by the Brueckner-Hartree-Fock (BHF) theory with realistic three-body forces and a generic bosonic self-interacting dark matter model, respectively. Based on the observational data, we determine the parameter space for XTE J1814-338 as a DNS, and find that only a halo stellar configuration with a high dark matter fraction is allowed. Furthermore, we predict other observable properties of XTE J1814-338 and provide robust lower bounds for these quantities.
papers.reason: Explores the possibility that the ultracompact millisecond pulsar XTE J1814-338 is a dark-matter-admixed neutron star using BHF theory.

papers.title: Algebraic models of alpha-cluster nuclei
papers.abstract: In this contribution I review the algebraic cluster model (ACM) for $\alpha$-conjugate nuclei with $A=4n$ and its extension to the cluster shell model (CSM) for $A=4n+x$ nuclei. The CSM describes the splitting of single-particles levels in a deformed field generated by the cluster of $\alpha$-particles. As an example, I discuss the energies, electromagnetic transitions and form factors of the neighboring nuclei $^{12}$C and $^{13}$C.
papers.reason: Reviews algebraic cluster models and cluster shell models for alpha-conjugate nuclei, including form factors for C-12 and C-13.

papers.title: An approximate separation of the electron and positron degrees of freedom in the Dirac-Heisenberg-Wigner formalism
papers.abstract: Here we study the quantum relativistic phase-space description of the Dirac field referred to as the Dirac--Heisenberg--Wigner (DHW) formalism. By applying a systematic expansion procedure in weak electromagnetic fields (compared to the Schwinger critical field) and slow temporal and long spatial scales (compared to the Compton scales), the 16 scalar phase-space functions of the DHW equations can be reduced to 8 scalars. By making a further change of variables, the equations can be interpreted as four evolution equations for the electron degrees of freedom and four for the positron degrees of freedom. We refer to these equations as the weakly coupled electron-positron (WCEP) limit of the DHW equations. Unlike the case after a Foldy--Wouthuysen transformation has been made, the electron and positron degrees of freedom remain weakly coupled. Naturally, further approximations can be made on the 4+4 equations so that only 4 equations for one particle species remain. Importantly, the expansion scheme can be carried out to all orders, in which case the reduced 4+4 model, contrary to other reduced models, will cover most quantum relativistic effects. Specifically, this includes vacuum polarization, a phenomenon that otherwise has been added phenomenologically, but here appears naturally as a feature of the general expansion scheme.
papers.reason: Derives a weakly coupled electron-positron limit of DHW equations including vacuum polarization, relevant to quantum relativistic phase-space methods.

papers.title: Two-loop matter power spectrum from FFTLog and kite integrals
papers.abstract: We present a fast and accurate method for computing the two-loop matter power spectrum in the Effective Field Theory of Large-Scale Structure (EFTofLSS). Using FFTLog, we decompose the linear power spectrum into complex power laws, reducing the two-loop corrections to cosmology-independent massless Feynman integrals of kite topology. A central numerical challenge is the evaluation of these integrals for complex powers with large imaginary parts, where the highly oscillatory integrands make accurate numerical evaluation particularly challenging. We overcome this difficulty using a Mellin--Barnes representation summed over a uniform lattice, achieving approximately ten digit precision even for large imaginary powers, with an error estimate for each integral. The resulting precomputed matrices allow the two-loop power spectrum to be evaluated for a new cosmology in a few milliseconds. Comparing with direct numerical integration, we find agreement at the $10^{-4}$ level relative to the power spectrum up to $k=0.2$ $h$Mpc$^{-1}$ after accounting for EFTofLSS counterterm contributions and FFTLog decomposition errors. The same framework extends to biased tracers and redshift-space distortions, providing the building blocks for general two-loop calculations in EFTofLSS. We make the code for evaluating the kite integrals publicly available, together with precomputed matrices and an implementation for the two-loop matter power spectrum as a concrete application. Our results can be directly incorporated into existing FFTLog-based codes for large-scale structure, extending their current one-loop capabilities to two loops within the same computational framework.
papers.reason: Develops fast computation methods for the two-loop matter power spectrum in the EFT of Large-Scale Structure using FFTLog.

papers.title: The signature-changing soft-gluon term as a possible source of non-planar $\zeta_2$ terms at small $x$ in the non-singlet quark-plus-antiquark splitting function
papers.abstract: A relation underlying resummations at small momentum fraction $x$ predicts the highest logarithms of quark-plus-antiquark flavor-difference splitting functions from lower orders. Complete three- and four-loop results violate it at third-highest logarithms by pi-squared terms suppressed for many colors, of unexplained origin and color structure. At four loops Moch and Vogt suggested a squared imaginary phase. We retain the signature-changing soft-gluon term also in positive signature in Kirschner and Lipatov's double-logarithmic equations for forward quark-antiquark scattering, without derivation, with their printed negative-signature sign and adjoint Born term. We show that the proposed equations reproduce both violations in full color for quark-plus-antiquark flavor differences at zero power of $x$, fixed coupling and first order in pi squared, for defining-representation quarks of special unitary groups with at least three colors. The proposed equations at third-highest logarithms use one wave per exchanged color and signature, the retained term at lowest-order strength as the positive-signature color-neutral channel's only new source of these violations, no such terms from gluons across the softest exchanged quark-antiquark pair at comparable or larger transverse momentum, and unchanged quark-pair normalization in the splitting function. This agreement gives three independent tests of one system with no continuous coefficient adjusted to the violations, although corresponding non-quartic quark-minus-antiquark terms are missed. In the proposed equations, the retained term weighted by this phase is a possible origin of both violations. The equations predict these full-color five-loop quark-plus-antiquark terms if the relation otherwise holds and no new source first acts at five loops. Confirmation would support the retained term as the origin of the violations through five loops.
papers.reason: Investigates signature-changing soft-gluon terms and pi-squared violations in small-x non-singlet quark splitting functions.

papers.title: A systematic study of hydrodynamic attractors in periodically driven systems at weak and strong couplings
papers.abstract: We study equilibration and hydrodynamic response in conformal systems undergoing periodic expansion and contraction along one spatial direction. Using strongly coupled holography (AdS/CFT), weakly coupled kinetic theories (relaxation-time approximation, scalar $\phi^4$ theory and the Yang--Mills sector of QCD effective kinetic theory) and hydrodynamics (Navier--Stokes, M\"uller--Israel--Stewart (MIS) and rBRSSS), we investigate the shear response to a periodic drive of varying amplitude $A$ and frequency $\omega$, both analytically in linear response and numerically. We find that, at the linear level, $A\ll 1$, periodically driven systems approach a cyclic attractor that in general differs from Navier--Stokes behaviour. This attractor is universal among kinetic theories and accurately described by MIS theory: for slow driving, $\omega \tau_\pi \ll 1$, where $\tau_\pi$ is the shear relaxation time, it approaches the Navier--Stokes limit, whereas for fast driving the shear stress saturates at its non-interacting (free-streaming) value. In strongly coupled holographic systems, the periodic drive excites non-hydrodynamic quasinormal modes, which produce a characteristic ringing in the approach to the cyclic attractor, in contrast to the purely exponential approach found in kinetic theories. This difference is a direct consequence of the distinct non-hydrodynamic spectra of the two classes of theories. Moreover, unlike in kinetic theory, the holographic response is sensitive to the curvature terms of second-order hydrodynamics. Over longer times, non-linear viscous heating, which is quadratic in the drive amplitude, raises the temperature and thereby lowers $\omega\tau_\pi$, since $\tau_\pi\sim 1/T$. This induces a slow drift of the cyclic attractor, which eventually converges towards Navier--Stokes hydrodynamics at asymptotically late times.
papers.reason: Studies equilibration and shear response in periodically driven conformal and kinetic systems, relevant to heavy-ion and hydrodynamic transport.

papers.title: Relativistic viscous hydrodynamics in the Density Frame for heavy-ion collisions
papers.abstract: We present a numerical study of relativistic viscous hydrodynamics in the Density Frame for boost-invariant flows in 2+1 dimensions. The Density Frame is a formulation of relativistic viscous hydrodynamics that is first order in time, requires no auxiliary fields, and has no non-hydrodynamic modes; the only parameters are the shear and bulk viscosities and the equation of state. We formulate the numerical method in terms of a discrete analog of the dissipative function, which guarantees that the discrete equations produce entropy on all length scales and leads to a remarkably robust algorithm. We test the method against the exact solution of kinetic theory in the relaxation time approximation with Gubser symmetry. In making this comparison, we clarify how the kinetic solution matches onto hydrodynamics: we organize the solution by the opacity and show how the Bjorken attractor passes onto the Gubser solution order by order in gradients. We then replace the hydrodynamic engine of the MUSIC code with the Density Frame, and compare the two for IP-Glasma initial conditions in Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 5.02$ TeV. The Density Frame smooths sharp gradients more rapidly. The largest differences arise in the bulk-viscous sector, where the bulk pressure in the Density Frame responds instantaneously to the flow, while in the M\"uller-Israel-Stewart-based MUSIC it relaxes over a finite time. With shear viscosity alone, the multiplicity, mean transverse momentum, and elliptic flow of final-state hadrons from the two codes are very similar. The Density Frame is now ready for a complete Bayesian analysis of heavy-ion data.
papers.reason: Develops relativistic viscous hydrodynamics in the Density Frame for heavy-ion collisions and compares with relaxation-time approximations.

papers.title: Two gluon fusion into a $\pi^0$, $\eta$, or $\eta'$ in a relatively weak magnetic field
papers.abstract: In this article, we investigate gluon fusion as a mechanism for neutral meson production ($\pi^0$, $\eta$, and $\eta'$), in the phenomenological context of heavy-ion collisions prior to thermalization, in which a large gluon multiplicity is expected, and when an intense background magnetic field is expected to arise. For this purpose, we computed the ratios of the emission probability rates in the presence of the background magnetic field as compared to vacuum (zero-field), as a function of transverse momenta $p_T$ and energy $\sqrt{s}$, close to midrapidity. Our theoretical results suggest a catalytic effect from the presence of the background magnetic field, that may enhance the neutral pion production by several orders of magnitude at very small energies $s \lesssim 1~\text{GeV}^2$, while the effect is negligible at larger energies $s\gtrsim 10~\text{GeV}^2$. In contrast, the $\eta$ and $\eta'$ production rates are nearly insensitive to the magnetic field presence (as compared to vacuum).
papers.reason: Calculates neutral meson production via gluon fusion in magnetic fields during heavy-ion collisions.

papers.title: Deconfinement in weak electric and magnetic fields
papers.abstract: We investigate the thermal deconfinement transition in weak electric and magnetic fields, describing the hadronic phase by a pion gas and the quark--gluon plasma by the MIT bag model. Besides the thermal response of each phase, we include the one-loop electromagnetic vacuum terms of quarks and charged pions, renormalized at a common scale that fixes the charge in the confined vacuum. With no fitting of the electromagnetic response, the critical temperature rises with the electric field and falls with the magnetic one. The electric curvature is of the same size as that obtained on the lattice, while the magnetic one is a few times larger. We discuss the dependence on quark mass and renormalization scale, and a large-$N_c$ organization of both curvatures, whose sum is independent of the vacuum terms and connects directly to perturbative QCD.
papers.reason: Investigates the thermal deconfinement transition in weak electric and magnetic fields using a pion gas and bag model.

papers.title: Quantum Popcorn: the shape of a phase transition bubble
papers.abstract: A quantum tunneling event in field theory is usually depicted as the materialization of a spherical bubble of true vacuum. The bubble appears at rest, and its profile is the time-symmetric slice of Coleman's bounce, the Euclidean solution that controls the decay rate. However, the bubble is spherical only in the leading semiclassical approximation: at the next order the configuration is a Gaussian ensemble of fluctuations around the bounce. We derive the wave functional of the field on the nucleation slice from the half-bounce path integral, and use it to compute the root-mean-square quadrupole moment of a bubble at nucleation. The relative deformation of the bubble wall radius $R$ is $\delta R/R\sim(\hbar/S_b)^{1/2}$, with $S_b$ the bounce action. Thus $\delta R/R\sim0.1$ for a typical cosmological phase transition with $S_b/\hbar\sim100$.
papers.reason: Computes the quantum fluctuations and quadrupole deformations of vacuum decay bubbles in first-order cosmological phase transitions.

papers.title: Leaking Sound Waves: Gravitational Waves From Dark Sectors Weakly Coupled to the Standard Model
papers.abstract: First-order phase transitions in a dark sector can produce an observable stochastic gravitational-wave background, and many models predicting such signals in current and future experiments have been explored. For moderately strong transitions, hydrodynamical simulations suggest that sound waves generated by the expansion and collisions of true-vacuum bubbles are the dominant source of gravitational waves. It is often assumed that these sound waves propagate only within the dark-sector fluid, while the impact of the visible sector is neglected. In this paper, we investigate the effects of a weak coupling between the dark and visible fluids on the resulting gravitational-wave signal. We adopt a phenomenological hydrodynamical description of two ultra-relativistic fluids, parametrizing their interactions without specifying an underlying microscopic model. We focus on the regime in which the coupling can be neglected during the phase transition but becomes relevant during the subsequent, longer-lasting period of sound wave propagation. Within this framework, we analytically show that, even if the bubble expansion initially affects only the dark fluid, sound waves can subsequently be induced in the visible sector. Using the sound-shell model, we find that, despite the additional sound waves generated in the visible sector, the total gravitational-wave signal sourced by both fluids is generally suppressed compared to the case of a completely decoupled dark sector. This suppression becomes more pronounced for larger interaction rates and a larger ratio of relativistic degrees of freedom in the visible sector to those in the dark sector. The coupling also modifies the shape of the gravitational-wave spectrum.
papers.reason: Examines gravitational waves from dark sector phase transitions with visible-sector coupling, which is adjacent to BSM dark portals.

papers.title: Primordial black holes and gravitational waves from aligned axion inflation
papers.abstract: We study the production of primordial black holes (PBHs) and scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) in aligned axion inflation through the transition between two stages of inflation. The first stage proceeds along a metastable trajectory and ends when this trajectory loses stability, causing the fields to turn towards the attractor of the second inflationary stage. During the transition, coupled adiabatic--entropy evolution produces a localized enhancement of the curvature power spectrum. We compute the PBH abundance from this spectrum assuming Gaussian primordial curvature perturbations and using the nonlinear compaction-function formalism with a spectrum-dependent collapse threshold and critical collapse. Representative benchmark solutions yield asteroid-mass PBHs with a potentially significant dark-matter abundance, together with an associated SIGW background.
papers.reason: Studies primordial black holes and scalar-induced gravitational waves from aligned axion inflation, adjacent to early universe BSM.

papers.title: Induced Lorentzian geometry from the fermionic quantum metric
papers.abstract: Quantum geometry is conventionally understood in parameter or momentum space and need not be related to a geometry in configuration space. Here we show for Dirac fermions in a background electromagnetic field that an induced Lorentzian geometry is generated from the fermionic quantum metric. We study a Lorentz covariant phase space worldline path integral construction, whose application of the adiabatic theorem onto spin degrees of freedom leads to the appearance of the Berry phase at $O(\hbar)$, and the quantum metric at $O(\hbar^2)$ in the worldline action. Both the Feynman and retarded/advanced propagators are examined in 3+1 and 2+1 dimensions, whose different on-shell implementations lead to related quantum metrics; QED/QED${}_3$ and condensed matter Dirac theory are considered. An effective theory is found by integrating out the momenta degrees of freedom, which gives rise to an emergent Lorentzian metric in configuration space, whose perturbation to the flat metric is dependent on the quantum metric and the background field strength. Apart from the spin degrees of freedom encoded into the Berry phase, the effective theory describes a scalar particle moving in the induced quantum geometry. Phenomenological applications to the covariant geometry are further studied using spectral holonomy in a gapped 3-dimensional Dirac material.
papers.reason: Derives an induced Lorentzian geometry from the quantum metric of Dirac fermions in background gauge fields.

papers.title: Nonthermal coalescence parameter of light nuclei production in pp collisions at LHC energies
papers.abstract: We study the light nucleus production in pp collisions at $\sqrt{s}=7$ and $13$~TeV reported by the ALICE Collaboration within the color string fragmentation framework. We adopt the Schwinger mechanism with string tension fluctuations as the particle production mechanism describing the $p_T$ spectrum. The approximately thermal behavior observed in the light-nucleus spectra motivates the use of a perturbative series expansion of the $q$-Gaussian string tension fluctuations around $q=1$. The resulting $p_T$ spectrum is expressed as a perturbative series expansion around the thermal distribution with nonthermal corrections given by Gamma distributions, providing closed forms for the effective temperature, moments, and cumulants. In the superstatistical framework, the associated temperature fluctuations show that the medium in which light nuclei are produced is out of equilibrium. Additionally, we derive closed formulas for the coalescence parameter at arbitrary order, which agree well with experimental data. Our results also show that the mass--temperature relation ($T_N/m_N \approx AT_A/m_A$) between the nucleons and nuclei is not preserved in the coalescence process.
papers.reason: Studies light nucleus production and coalescence parameters in pp collisions using superstatistics and string tension fluctuations.

papers.title: Updated $\Sigma_{c}$ excitation spectrum including the $2P$- and $1F$-wave fine structures
papers.abstract: In order to study the new $\Sigma_{c}$ baryons observed by the LHCb collaboration recently, we update the previously predicted $\Sigma_{c}$ excitation spectrum by extending the excited states up to the highly excited $2P$- and $1F$-wave states. The calculation is performed in the framework of the relativized quark model and Gaussian expansion method by considering the mixing effect. The radially and orbitally excited states in the calculation are determined by the truncation convention proposed in this work and the mechanism of the heavy-quark dominance. The contribution of each Hamiltonian term to the energy levels is precisely calculated by using the two-step Gaussian expansion method. Then, the concerned $\Sigma_{c}$ states are obtained and the $\Sigma_{c}$ excitation spectrum including the $2P$- and $1F$-wave fine structures is established. Based on these, several important topics are discussed and analyzed, including the root-mean-square radii, off-diagonal matrix elements, mixing effect, fine structures and assignments of the newly observed $\Sigma_{c}(2800)^{0}$, $\Sigma_{c}(2900)^{0}$ and $\Sigma_{c}(3200)^{0}$ states. Meanwhile, it is found that the approximate decoupling phenomenon emerges in different $nL$-wave groups. This implies the reasonability of the truncation convention and is of great significance for further improving the calculation scheme for all the baryon spectra. Moreover, it is demonstrated that in the very high-lying $nL$-wave groups such as the $1F$-wave group, the energy level gaps become small even degenerate, and each of the baryon states has a big radius and therefore a loosely bound structure. In addition, by examining the experimental and calculated data, we suggest more precise experiments to search for more $\Sigma_{c}$ baryon states in the predicted $1P$- and $2P$-wave fine structures whose central energies are around 2822 and 3210 MeV, respectively.
papers.reason: Calculates the relativized quark model excitation spectrum and fine structure for Sigma_c baryons including 2P and 1F waves.

papers.title: The role of spin polarization in event-by-event fluctuations
papers.abstract: The event-by-event initial state fluctuations constitute a critical physical quantity for understanding the dynamics of high-energy heavy-ion collisions. Due to the extremely limited available experimental data of such fluctuations, it is difficult to constrain or direct the characterization of the underlying initial state properties. This work constrains the correlation function between the initial eccentricity and the asymmetry by employing a parton distribution function that incorporates spin polarization induced by thermal vorticity and thermal shear. Based on the kinetic theory calculations, we found that the asymmetry fluctuations considering spin polarization have a significant splitting effect compared to those without spin polarization. These splitting exhibit pronounced system size and energy dependence. Moreover, the ratios of correlation function display similar system size and energy dependence--particularly in the low-temperature regime ($T \lesssim$ 0.12 GeV). These results suggest that spin polarization may serve as a useful constraint method for the event-by-event initial state fluctuations of heavy-ion collisions.
papers.reason: Investigates the effect of spin polarization induced by thermal vorticity on initial-state eccentricity fluctuations in heavy-ion collisions.

papers.title: Numerical evaluation of one-loop integrals using quadrature rules
papers.abstract: We introduce a numerical quadrature algorithm with stretched exponential convergence to evaluate one-loop integrals in dimensional regularisation in the causal Loop Tree Dual (cLTD) representation. The key feature that makes this possible is the fact that for Euclidean kinematics all singularities of the cLTD integrand lie on a compact set in loop momentum space. We prove that our algorithm admits a stretched exponential convergence with the number of integrand evaluations, and we illustrate it by evaluating triangle, box and pentagon integrals at selected Euclidean kinematics points. We benchmark our implementation against analytic results as well as results obtained via Monte Carlo integration. We also provide a proof of concept that our algorithm can be extended to physical kinematics after subtraction of threshold singularities.
papers.reason: Introduces a numerical quadrature algorithm with stretched exponential convergence for one-loop integrals using causal Loop Tree Duality.

papers.title: Reconstruct everything everywhere all at once: An end-to-end model for future colliders
papers.abstract: We present the Reconstruct Everything Model (REM), an end-to-end multitask model for sparse, multimodal sensor data, demonstrated in high-energy physics. To our knowledge, REM is the first demonstration of a single learned framework simultaneously reconstructing multiple particle types directly from hit-level measurements across the silicon tracker, calorimeters, and muon system in a full simulation. It performs hit assignment, particle identification, kinematic regression, and resonance reconstruction without externally reconstructed tracks or calorimeter clusters as inputs. REM improves particle-reconstruction efficiency and purity and jet-energy resolution relative to both conventional and machine-learned particle-flow approaches. In diboson events, the learned resonance reconstruction improves W/Z mass separation relative to conventional jet reconstruction. These results demonstrate a reconstruction chain from detector hits to particles to resonances, with potential applications to structured prediction in other large-scale, sparse, multimodal sensor systems.
papers.reason: Presents an end-to-end neural network (REM) for simultaneous particle reconstruction from hit-level detector data in colliders.

papers.title: Topological Multi-Natural Inflation
papers.abstract: We investigate topological inflation in minimal multi-natural inflation, in which the axion potential consists of two cosine terms. Focusing on the high-scale regime, we perform a systematic parameter scan for representative ratios of the two periods and identify regions consistent with current constraints on the scalar spectral index and tensor-to-scalar ratio, including those from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope. The interplay of the two harmonics allows departures from the quartic hilltop limit and accommodates the higher spectral index favored by recent cosmological data combinations. We characterize the hilltop and near-inflection-point branches and analyze the associated vacuum structure and domain-wall properties. We also discuss a symmetry-breaking origin of the required domain walls when the inflaton is the angular component of a complex scalar field. We identify regions in which the observational constraints and the adopted criteria for topological inflation are simultaneously satisfied, including regions with a sub-Planckian axion decay constant. Our results show that the observational tension encountered in the minimal quartic double-well model need not extend to topological inflation in a minimal multi-natural axion potential.
papers.reason: Investigates topological inflation in multi-natural axion potentials with cosmological constraints from ACT and Planck.

papers.title: Characterizing $\pT$-differential Radial-Flow Fluctuations in Au+Au Collisions at FAIR with a Multi-Phase Transport Model
papers.abstract: We report the first predictions of the transverse-momentum ($\pT$)-differential radial-flow fluctuation observable, $\vzpT$, in Au+Au collisions at the top SIS100 energy, $\snn=4.9$~GeV, which will be available at the FAIR accelerator complex. Radial flow and its fluctuations are studied for different centrality intervals and reference-$\pT$ selections to investigate the properties and robustness of the calculated long-range correlation. $\vzpT$ displays a characteristic evolution from negative values at low $\pT$ to positive values at higher $\pT$. The integrated $v_0$, obtained with different reference-$\pT$ intervals, follows a common trend, with an approximately inverse-square-root dependence on the inclusive charged-particle multiplicity ($\nch$). The $\vzpT$ signal changes little when the pseudorapidity gap is varied between 0.2 and 0.8, or when the edges of the reference-$\pT$ interval are varied, in the bulk region. For identified particles, the pion and proton $\vzpT$ are ordered at low $\pT$, qualitatively similar to the mass ordering seen at higher energies. However, unlike at higher collision energies, $\vzpT$ does not exhibit constituent-quark scaling, so the results do not support an interpretation in terms of partonic collectivity. These results provide constraints on the evolution of radial correlations toward lower collision energies and motivate comparisons with complementary observables to clarify their connection to collective dynamics.
papers.reason: Simulates transverse-momentum fluctuations in heavy-ion collisions at FAIR, touching nuclear dynamics but focused on QGP/heavy-ion collectivity.

papers.title: Combinatorial Residual Network: a decay-chain-aware classifier without explicit jet assignment
papers.abstract: Final states with several jets from the decays of heavy particles pose a combinatorial problem, since the jets must be assigned, at least implicitly, to their parent particles. We describe the Combinatorial Residual Network (CoReNet), a classifier that encodes the assumed decay chain of the final state in its architecture. CoReNet builds its event representation level by level along the decay hierarchy, evaluates every jet assignment hypothesis with weights shared across objects, and combines the hypotheses with learned weights using residual networks. The exchange symmetries of the decay are built into the construction, the size of the network does not depend on the number of hypotheses, and the network is trained with the classification loss alone, without generator-level jet assignments. The architecture was developed for the $b\bar{b}b\bar{b}$ final state and has been used in several CMS searches. On fast-simulation samples of Higgs boson pair production in the $b\bar{b}b\bar{b}$ final state against QCD multijet production, CoReNet with 1508 trainable parameters performs well above kinematic baselines and trains in minutes on a single GPU. Its hypothesis weights select the truth-matched jet pairing in most of the signal events in which it is defined, although no assignment target is used in training. Since only the encoded decay chain is specific to the final state, the construction carries over to other topologies, which we test with $HH \to b\bar{b}W^+W^-$ against semileptonic $t\bar{t}$. There, encoding the decay chain of the background as well as that of the signal further improves the classification, at a cost of about $10^3$ parameters. In both final states its performance is comparable to that of a state-of-the-art transformer-based network more than two orders of magnitude larger.
